verdict.rationale: Pylon ships customer-facing AI Support Agents, so a guardrails story is a fair question for it. However, no evidence documents a guardrail that limits answers to the knowledge base or returns a safe decline for off-knowledge questions. The nearby material is all adjacent: deflecting questions "using content", natural-language runbooks a user could write guardrail instructions into, persona tuning, simulation testing, post-hoc QA rubrics, and controlling which issues the agent touches. None of these is a documented anti-hallucination or decline behavior.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, guardrails stop the agent from inventing policies, prices, or promises — off-knowledge questions get a safe decline, not a guess
